conviction_note: Two negatives sum to -2.0: a Chinese-press report (single source) that Yixianghua lending stopped at the end of June, and an unprovisioned RMB3.43bn related-party receivable now under a new auditor. I emit -1.0, half the sum, for three reasons: the bar is unsourced, so every size is capped; the stock sits at about 0.07x book, with a market cap near one sixth of the receivable, so most of the distress is visibly priced; and confirmed earnings releases have moved this name only about 2-4%.
bar: unsourced. There is no retrievable consensus and the company gives no guidance (Q1 release: 'no guidance'; management only said it expects 'more meaningful profitability gains in the second half'). I used Q1 2026 net revenue of RMB915.1m as a sequential proxy bar (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1631761/000121390026072295/ea029591401ex99-1.htm). Every size here is capped because of this.
positioning_check: Short interest about 0.7% of float, 1.05 days to cover, 42,324 shares. Source is the Benzinga short-interest page via a sweep search snippet, with no settlement date shown (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/YRD/short-interest). The Nasdaq short-interest API returned 503 on 2026-09-29. Not crowded, so squeeze risk is low, but Ning Tang owns about 82%, which leaves a free float of roughly 16m ADS (about $15m). Skew is null because the chain is unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes). Put/call OI ratio is 0.14 on 360 contracts, which says nothing. The market's own statement is the price itself: -85.7% from the 52-week high, about 0.07x book equity of $1.27bn, and a market cap of about $82m against $356m cash plus $74m investments.

findings.finding: Chinese financial press (理财周刊 via Tencent News, 2026-07-02) reports, citing other media, that Yixianghua's funding partners stopped working with it after the CreditEase wealth-product redemption halt and that the platform was 'forced to suspend lending at end-June, keeping only referral and membership business'. If true, the Q2 release's volume figures and any H2 commentary will contradict management's June 25 line about 'more meaningful profitability gains in the second half'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline history is untrustworthy (6-K noise; the +59.65% on 2026-07-02 was a buyback). Rebuilt from the four confirmed releases in the baseline list: 2025-08-22 +1.99, 2025-11-26 +3.76, 2026-03-20 -2.96, Q1 on 2026-06-25/26 +0.91. Median abs about 2.5%. This includes the Q1 print that showed revenue -41% YoY and a RMB495m loss, which the stock took with a small move. Volume and outlook shocks have not been paid for large on print days; the de-rating came from the CreditEase news flow (weekly close about $2.07 mid-May to $1.36 by end-May).
findings.why_not_priced: Chinese-only and second-hand ('据媒体报道'). English coverage of the last print (TipRanks, 'Earnings Call Signals Early Turnaround'; Investing.com, 'narrows loss... as credit costs ease') carries the stabilisation narrative, and there has been no company 6-K since 2026-07-02. If the lending halt were priced, it would be hard to tell apart from what the price already shows: ADS -35% from the post-buyback spike and trading far below net cash. So the unpriced part is at most the gap between 'stabilising' and 'halted' in the outlook, not the distress itself.
findings.independence: none. The same Tencent-hosted search cluster repeats the claim but traces back to this article. The regulatory interview of 2026-03-13 and the 24% APR cap context (https://www.huxiu.com/article/4843114.html, 2026-03-18) explain why funding would be fragile, but they do not confirm a halt.

findings.finding: Amounts due from the controlling shareholder and its affiliates rose from RMB2.97bn (2025-12-31) to RMB3.43bn (2026-03-31) with no provision ('currently performing in accordance with their contractual terms'). The company switched auditor from Wei, Wei & Co. to Marcum Asia effective 2026-06-01, days after CreditEase Wealth halted redemptions, and by August the affiliate's liquidation plan was still unpublished while claims were reported trading at about 30% of net principal. The late Q2 date (Sept 30 vs Aug 22 last year) is consistent with this balance being re-examined, which raises the risk of an impairment or a changed disclosure in the release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior related-party impairment at this company to measure against. The nearest line is the 2026-05-27 statement distancing Yiren from the affiliates' products (baseline row 2026-05-27, +3.5%), which followed the halt and did not stop the slide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. A market cap of about $82m against a $497m receivable and $356m of cash says investors already treat the balance, and some of the cash, as impaired or captive. What is not priced is the accounting event itself: a quantified write-down would produce a very large headline loss on a retail-heavy ADS. A one-off with no path to guidance is sized at a fraction.
findings.independence: Auditor change: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1631761/000121390026063134/ea029272501ex99-1.htm (2026-06-01). CreditEase Wealth plan still unpublished and claims at about 30% of net principal: https://finance.sina.com.cn/roll/2026-08-11/doc-inimwyqt7620292.shtml (2026-08-11, snippet_only, fetch returned 503). Zero-provision point also in https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20260702A090J400, which is the same document as finding 1 for that sub-point.

outside_window.finding: The ADS has closed under $1.00 on weekly bars since mid-September 2026 (0.983 week of 2026-09-14, 0.943 on 2026-09-29). An NYSE below-$1 continued-listing notice needs a 30-trading-day average under $1, which cannot be reached before about late October, so it falls outside the exit window.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR 6-Ks after 2026-07-02: none. No NT filing, no NYSE notice, no buyback-execution disclosure (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001631761.json)

H1 2026 dividend: the policy is at least 10% of anticipated H1 net income, and Q1 alone lost RMB495m, so no dividend is implied. The market is not expecting last year's $0.20/ADS (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/yrd/dividend/)
Buyback execution: the $20m program was authorised 2026-07-02, but ADS turnover is about $40k/day since, so open-market execution through the window is necessarily tiny. No disclosure found
Consensus Q2 revenue/EPS: none retrievable from free sources
Yixianghua user complaints (Heimao, Zhihu, 36kr): complaint volume is about forced disbursement and high fees, not about an inability to borrow, so they neither confirm nor refute the lending halt
Going-private / Ning Tang proposal after he reached 82% on 2026-06-08: no filing or report found
baseline_tension: No skew to agree or disagree with. Both negatives point the way the price has already gone (-86% from the high, about 0.07x book, below net cash), so most of what I found is already in the price, and I emit half the findings' sum.
lessons_applied: Rule 6: the bar is unsourced (no consensus, no guide), so both findings are capped small. Lending halt cut from -2.0 to -1.5.
Rule 5: the lending-halt finding rests on a second-hand press report ('据媒体报道'), not a company or counterparty document. That is another reason it stays small.
Rule 2: the related-party receivable is a one_off with no path to guidance, and the market cap is already below it. Cut from -1.0 to -0.5.
Rebuilt the base rate from the four confirmed releases (median abs about 2.5%) rather than the 6-K history. This caps the reaction, and expected_move is cut from -2.0 to -1.0.
Rule 3 and the pessimism lesson: both findings agree with a price already far below net cash, so expected_move is kept at half the sum.
Rule 7: short interest checked (0.7%, 1.05 DTC). Not crowded, so no squeeze haircut is needed, though the 82% insider holding leaves a very thin float.
